name: Trivandrum Boli
description: A traditional sweet associated with Thiruvananthapuram.

name: Travancore-style biryani
description: The city's mutton biryani tradition, with one long-running biryani house often cited as the benchmark.

name: Karimeen pollichathu
description: Pearl spot fish marinated in spices, wrapped in banana leaf and fried or grilled in coconut oil, a toddy-shop favourite served with kappa.

name: Kallummakkaya (mussels) curry
description: Green mussels from the Malabar coast, cooked in curries or stuffed and fried. A signature of Mappila cooking that is popular in Kollam.

name: Fish moilee
description: Fish simmered in a mild coconut-milk gravy, usually eaten with appam.

name: Kollam dum biryani
description: A slow-cooked biryani sealed to hold its spices, a local favourite.

name: Aranmula Valla Sadya
description: A ritual vegetarian feast of dozens of dishes served on plantain leaves at the Sree Parthasarathy Temple, Aranmula, during the boat-race season.

name: Kuttanadan duck curry (Tharavu curry)
description: The best-known dish of Kuttanad, a deep-green duck curry of coriander, pepper, coconut milk and green chillies, often cooked in earthenware.

name: Kuttanadan duck roast
description: A spiced duck roast, a Kuttanad speciality eaten with appam, puttu or parotta.

name: Meen mappas
description: Fish in a mild coconut-milk gravy, associated with Syrian Christian cooking in Kuttanad.

name: Kakka (freshwater clam) roast
description: Backwater clams roasted with spices and grated coconut, a Kuttanad speciality.

name: Pidi and chicken curry
description: Small steamed rice dumplings served with chicken in a roasted-coconut gravy, a Christian-home classic that locals call a perfect pairing.

name: Kottayam fish dishes
description: Central Travancore fish cooking: molly, mappas, peera and spicy fish curry with boiled tapioca.

name: Panampani
description: A traditional drink served at the end of old Christian wedding feasts in Kottayam.

name: Kottayam Uzhunnada
description: A crispy snack of black gram, tapioca flour and salt, traditional to central Kerala.

name: Ellum kappayum
description: Beef on the bone cooked with tapioca, a hill-country favourite.

name: Kappa biryani
description: Tapioca layered with spiced beef in the style of a biryani.

name: Idiyirachi
description: Sun-dried beef, a preserved speciality of the Idukki hills.

name: Kochi Christian sweets
description: Achappam, kuzhalappam, cheeda, vattayappam and kinnathappam, a group of festive snacks and sweets of Kochi.

name: Kurukku kalan
description: A thick yoghurt curry with toasted banana, eaten with hot rice, one of Kochi's vegetarian specialities.

name: Thrissur Pooram sadya
description: The festive banana-leaf feast tied to Thrissur Pooram, which some say has the best variety in Kerala.

name: Vellayappam
description: A soft, bowl-shaped rice pancake especially associated with the area around the Basilica of Our Lady of Dolours.

name: Thrissur street snacks
description: Pazhampori and vada at Pothanicaud, kappa biryani and kozhukkatta at Ollur, parippu vada at Mannuthy.

name: Palakkad Iyer cuisine
description: A largely vegetarian, low-oil cooking tradition built on molagootal, molakushyam, rasam and long-brined mango and gooseberry pickles.

name: Palada pradhaman
description: A rich milk-and-rice-ada dessert, one of the signature sweets of Palakkad Iyer kitchens.

name: Meen pathiri
description: Fish curry layered between rice breads and steamed, one of the best-known Mappila dishes.

name: Kozhi thalayana
description: A chicken dish stuffed with boiled eggs, wrapped in dough and baked, showing clear Arab influence.

name: Mappila samosa
description: A snack distinguished by its spiced meat filling.

name: Ghee rice (neichoru)
description: Ghee-cooked rice, a staple for guests and celebrations in Mappila homes.

name: Kozhikodan halwa
description: The city's thick, glossy sweet, sold along Mittayi Theruvu (Sweet Meat Street). Arab traders are believed to have brought the idea to the Malabar coast.

name: Kozhikode biryani
description: A fragrant biryani of kaima rice, tender meat and a spice blend, described as a fancier cousin of Thalassery biryani.

name: Nannari sharbat
description: A cooling drink made from sarsaparilla root, a traditional refresher.

name: Paniya crab curry
description: A crab curry from the Paniya community, whose traditional diet relied on river fish, crab and tapioca.

name: Bamboo rice porridge
description: A tribal delicacy of Wayanad made with bamboo rice.

name: Tapioca with fish curry
description: Boiled tapioca eaten with a spicy fish curry, a Wayanad staple.

name: Thalassery dum biryani
description: Kannur's headline dish: a dum biryani made with short-grain kaima rice instead of basmati.

name: Unnakkaya
description: Plantain stuffed with sweetened coconut and fried in ghee, found in every Kannur tea shop.

name: Thalassery mussel dishes
description: Green mussel preparations, a Thalassery speciality, supported by local mussel farming.

name: Ari pathiri
description: A thin rice-flour flatbread cooked on a griddle, a staple of Malabar cuisine in the north.

name: Upperi (pickle)
description: In Kasaragod usage upperi means pickle, not thoran as in central Kerala, a small sign of the district's own food vocabulary.

name: Kaliyoottu
description: Kaliyoottu also known as Kali natakam (literally means Kali play) is a ritualistic performing art popular in Thiruvananthapuram and Kanniyakumari districts of southern Kerala, India. It is a folk art related to the battle between Bhadrakali and the asura Darika.

name: Nishagandhi Dance Festival
description: Nishagandhi Dance Festival, organised by the Kerala Tourism Department, is a one-week festival of classical dances held annually in the Nishagandhi amphitheatre, Kanakakkunnu Palace, Thiruvananthapuram. It usually happens in the months of January - February, every year.

name: Balaramapuram handlooms
description: Balaramapuram handlooms are part of a centuries-old weaving tradition in Thiruvananthapuram. Balaramapuram handloom is a part of Thiruvananthapuram's fashion and textile heritage.

name: Ramanattam
description: Ramanattam is a temple art in Kerala, India. The dance drama presents the story of Rama in a series of eight plays and was created under the patronage of Veera Kerala Varma (AD 1653–1694) alias Kottarakkara Thampuran.

name: Kollam Pooram
description: Kollam Pooram is a ten-day festival held every year in April in Kollam City in the Indian state of Kerala. The festival attracts a large number of people from all parts of the state and is organised in connection with the annual festival of the Asramam Sree Krishna Swamy Temple at Kollam's Asramam Maidan.

name: Kalidasa Kalakendram
description: Kalidasa Kalakendram is a professional drama theatrical group founded by O. Madhavan, a well-known Malayalam theatre director, in Kollam, Kerala. The group was founded on 25 January 1963 as a society under the parent organisation, Paul Foundation.

name: Theyyannam
description: Theyyannam is a traditional ritual folk art form that exists among the Pulaya, Kurava and Paraya communities of the central Travancore region in Kerala, India. It is mainly performed in Mavelikkara, Pandalam and some other parts of Alappuzha district.

name: Payippadu Vallam Kali
description: Payippad Boat Races, also known as Payippad Vallaarattu, or Jalotsavam, is a three-day water festival including the famous boat races, conducted in Payippad Lake, 6 km from Haripad of Kerala state in south India. There is a close relation between this Payippadu Vallam Kali and Haripad Sree Subrahmanya Swamy temple.

name: Malapulayattam
description: Malapulayattam also known as Chikk Attam is a tribal dance performed by the Malapulayan tribals of Idukki district in Kerala, as part of worshiping the deities Mariamman, Kaliyamman and Meenakshi in their caste-related festivals. This ritualistic dance is also performed in public spaces outside Idukki as part of…

name: Marayoor jaggery
description: The Marayoor jaggery is a variety of jaggery (non-centrifugal cane sugar) made from fresh sugarcane juice in the Indian state of Kerala. It is an agri-product manufactured from sugarcane which is a common and widely cultivated crop in Marayoor and Kanthalloor Grama panchayaths of Devikulam taluk, Idukki district…

name: Chendamangalam saree
description: Chendamangalam Saree is a traditional hand woven cotton sari from Chendamangalam, Ernakulam district of Kerala. This saree is part of the Chendamangalam Handloom tradition of Kerala.

name: Aluva Sivarathri festival
description: Aluva Sivarathri Festival is the Sivarathri celebrated in Aluva Mahadeva Temple in Aluva, Kochi in the state of Kerala, India The celebration of Sivarathri in Aluva is very famous in Kerala. The month of Kumbham is noted for the Sivarathri festival which falls in February – March.

name: Vazhakulam pineapple
description: Vazhakulam pineapple is the term used to refer to the pineapple produced in the Vazhakulam area in Kerala. The appellation "Vazhakulam" has been registered as Geographical Indication No.

name: Kuthampully saree
description: Kuthampully saree is a type of sari traditionally made by weavers from Kuthampully village in Thiruvilwamala Grama Panchayat of Thrissur district of Kerala state in India. The Kuthampully Saree is distinguished by its Saree borders.

name: Chembai Sangeetholsavam
description: Chembai Sangeetholsavam is an annual Carnatic music festival held in Guruvayur by the Guruvayur Devaswom (similar to the Thyagaraja Aradhana at Thiruvaiyaru) in memory of Chembai Vaidyanatha Bhagavatar, a Carnatic classical musician and a devotee of Guruvayurappan.

name: Uthralikavu Pooram
description: Uthralikkavu Pooram (ഉത്രാളിക്കാവ്) is a festival held at Shri Rudhiramahakalikav (ശ്രീ രുധിരമഹാകാളികാവ്) temple situated at Wadakkanchery in Thalappilly taluk of Thrissur district in Kerala, South India. The temple is famed for its Pooram festival held during February / March every year.

name: Arattupuzha Pooram
description: The oldest pooram (temple festival) in Kerala, the Arattupuzha Pooram, is held at the Arattupuzha Temple in Thrissur for a period of seven days each year. Believers say that at this 'conclave', all Gods and Goddesses gather during the time period of the Pooram.

name: Peruvanam Pooram
description: Peruvanam Pooram is one of the most popular temple festivals of the South Indian state of Kerala. It is held at Peruvanam Temple in Cherpu, Thrissur District.

name: Thirumandhamkunnu Pooram
description: Thirumandhamkunnu Pooram is an important temple festival of Central Malabar, Kerala, India. Thriumandhamkunnu Temple is said to be one among the three important Bhagavathi temples of Kerala, the others being Kodungallur and Panayannarkavu.

name: Kodungallur Bharani festival
description: Kodungallur Bharani festival is a yearly festival dedicated to the goddess Bhadrakali of Kodungallur Kurumba Bhagavathy temple held between the Bharani days of months Kumbham and Meenam of the Malayalam calendar. This period usually falls between the months of March and April in Roman calendar.

name: Chengalikodan Nendran Banana
description: Changalikodan Nendran Banana, or simply Changalikodan, is a banana variety originating and cultivated in Thrissur District in Kerala, India. Changalikodan, now are cultivated on the banks of the Bharathapuzha river.

name: Kanyarkali
description: Kanniyar Kali is a folk dance ritual performed in the temples of villages in the taluks of Alathur and Chittur, Palakkad district, Kerala, India. The event is usually a part of Vishu celebrations, occurring after the Vela (village fair) in the months of April and May.

name: Poothan and Thira
description: Poothan and Thira is a ritualistic folk art performed mainly in the Valluvanad region (present-day Palakkad district) of central Kerala in India, in which people dance in costumes representing Poothan is the lieutenant of Kali, and Thira, the goddess Kali, to the accompaniment of drummers. Thudi a small drum using…

name: Irula Nritham
description: Irula Nritham (also known as Irular Nritham) is a traditional tribal dance form performed by the Irula community of southern India, particularly in the Attappadi region of Palakkad district in Kerala.

name: Tattamangalam Kuthira Vela
description: Tattamangalam Kuthira Vela or Angadi Vela is a festival conducted in a small village called Tathamangalam in the Palakkad District of Kerala, south India. Kuthira means "horse" and Vela means "festival" in the Malayalam language.

name: Chinakkathoor Pooram
description: Chinakkathoor Pooram is a festival held annually at the Chinakkathoor Bhagavathi temple at Palappuram in Palakkad district of Kerala, India. A huge procession of 27 festooned tuskers is the highlight of the festival.

name: Manappullikavu Vela
description: Discover the spiritual heart of Palakkad at Sree Manappullikkavu Bhagavathy Temple, a renowned Hindu temple dedicated to the powerful Badrakali. Rooted in the sacred moolasthanam of West Yakkara, the divine presence of Manapulli Amma extends in all directions, with revered temples in East Yakkara, Kallikkad, and…

name: Palakkadan Matta rice
description: Matta rice (also known as Palakkadan/Kerala/Rose Matta rice, Kaje Rice in Karnataka, or Kuththarisi), Kannada: ಕಜೆ, ಕುಚಲಕ್ಕಿ, Tamil: குத்தரிசி, lit. 'Kuttarici') is an indigenous variety of rice grown in Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts of Karnataka, Palakkad district of Kerala,a traditional red parboiled rice…

name: Navara rice
description: Navara rice is one of the many types of rice found in India, and is a unique grain plant in the Oryza group. It originated in Palakkad (Palghat) district Kerala, where it is regarded as endemic.

name: Vairankode Vela
description: The Vairankode Festival, also known as Vairankode Vela or Vairankode Theeyattulsavam, is an annual celebration held at the Vairankode Bhagavathy Temple near Thirunavaya in the Malappuram district, Kerala. It is dedicated to the goddess Bhadra Kaali.

name: Kottakkal pooram
description: Kottakkal pooram is a temple festival in Sree Viswambhara Temple, Kottakkal, Malappuram District in Kerala, India.

name: Edayur chilli
description: The Edayur chilli is a variety of chilli mainly grown in the Indian state of Kerala. The Edayur chilli is a local cultivar primarily grown in specific regions of Kerala's Malappuram district.

name: Krishnanattam
description: Krishnanattam is a temple art in Kerala, India. It is a dance drama and presents the story of Krishna in a series of eight plays and was created by Manaveda (1585–1658 AD), the then Zamorin Raja of Kozhikode in northern Kerala.

name: Thacholikali
description: Thacholikali is a folk art performed during the Mandala Utsavam, forty-one day annual festival at the Lokanarkavu Bhagavathy Temple. Lokanarkavu temple is situated 5 km from Vatakara, a small town in Kerala state of South India.

name: Sargaalaya Crafts Village
description: Sargaalaya is a 20-acre (8.1 ha) arts and crafts village in Iringal, near Vatakara in the Kozhikode district of Kerala, India. It was established at a cost of around 15 crores on 19 February 2011 by The Kerala Tourism Department.

name: Kambara dance
description: The Kambara nritham or Kambara dance is a folk dance performed by the Adiyan tribe of Wayanad, a northern district of the state of Kerala. In this artform, men sing folk songs and play wind and percussion instruments, while women dance near the paddies where saplings are collected.

name: Wayanad Jeerakasala rice
description: Wayanad Jeerakasala rice is a variety of traditional, non-basmati, medium-grained aromatic rice with golden yellow colour, mainly grown in the Indian state of Kerala. It is a common and widely cultivated crop in Wayanad district.

name: Wayanad Gandhakasala rice
description: Gandhakasala rice is a variety of rice cultivated by the farmers in Wayanad District in Kerala. This is a scented variety of rice grown mostly by the members of the tribal communities in Panamaram, Sultan Bathery, and Mananthavady areas in Wayanad.

name: Wayanad Robusta coffee
description: Wayanad Robusta coffee (also spelt Wayanaad Robusta) is a robusta coffee (Coffea canephora) grown in the Wayanad district of the Indian state of Kerala. It was granted a geographical indication (GI) tag in 2019, with the Coffee Board of India as the registered proprietor.

name: Bappiriyan Theyyam
description: Bappiriyan Theyyam (also spelled as Bappirian) is a theyyam performed in North Malabar region in Kerala, India. It is a type of Mappila Theyyam.

name: Devakkoothu
description: Devakkoothu also spelled as Devakoothu is a ritualistic dance performed in Kerala, India. It is the only theyyam performed by a woman.

name: Kuttichathan Theyyam
description: Kuttichathan Theyyam also known as Sasthappan Theyyam is a Theyyam performed in the North Malabar region of Kerala state, India. It honors Kuttichathan, an important guardian deity in Malabari Hindu folkore.

name: Kuttiattoor Mango
description: The 'Kuttiattoor' mango or Kuttiattoor Manga, is a mango cultivar primarily grown in the village of Kuttiattoor, Kannur district of Kerala, India. 'Nambiar maanga', 'Kannapuram maanga', 'Kunjimangalam manga' and 'Vadakkumbhagam manga,' are the variations of the same name.

name: Kasaragod saree
description: A Kasaragod saree is a type of traditional cotton sari made by weavers belonging to the Saliya community in the Kasaragod district of Kerala. They are handmade and durable.

name: Aranmula kannadi
description: Aranmula Kannadi, meaning the Aranmula mirror, is a handmade, metal-alloy, first surface mirror made in Aranmula, a small town in Pathanamthitta in the state of Kerala, India. The mirrors received a geographical indication (GI) tag in 2005.

name: Payyannur Pavithra ring
description: Payyannur Pavithra Mothiram is a kind of gold ring worn by Indians for its ritualistic value. This holy ring is worn during the rituals of pithru bali, or the prayer for the dead ancestors of the person.

name: Pulikali
description: Pulikali is a recreational folk art from the state of Keralam, India, performed during Onam, an annual harvest festival. The performance revolves around the theme of tiger hunting.

name: Kummatti
description: Kummatti is a district in Raahe, Finland. It was countryside until the 1960s; the first apartment house was built in 1966.

name: Chavittu Nadakam
description: Chavittu Nadakam is a form of theatre originating in Kerala state in India, supposedly the city of Fort Kochi, associated with the Latin Christians of the region. It is noted for its flamboyant make-up discipline, elaborate costuming and detail to gesture and body movements.

name: Yakshagana
description: Yakshagana is a traditional stage performance and semi-classical Indian dance, drama, found in Tulunadu, that is Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kasaragod district and Uttara Kannada, Shimoga and western parts of Chikmagalur districts, in the state of Karnataka and in Kasaragod district in Kerala that combines dance,…

name: Alleppey coir
description: Alleppy Coir refers to the Coir products made in Ambalappuzha and Cherthala Taluks of Alappuzha district, in the state of Kerala, India. Coir production in this region dates back to as early as 1859.

name: Poorakkali
description: Poorakkali (meaning Festival Performance) is a traditional dance ritual performed by men during the nine-day Pooram Thiyya festival in Bhagavathy temples across North Malabar in Kerala State of south India. The Pooram festival begins with the Karthika asterism and concludes with the Pooram asterism of the month of…

name: Theyyam
description: Theyyam also known as Kaliyattam, is an Indian ritual practiced in the North Malabar Region of Kerala and some parts of neighbouring Karnataka. It involves extended singing of ritual songs related to the performing Theyyam and ceremonial preparations that typically span 8 to 10 hours.

name: Kaipad rice
description: Kaipad fields are salinity-prone natural organic rice cultivation fields in the northern districts of Kerala, India. The traditional kaipad system of rice cultivation is an integrated organic farming system in which rice cultivation and aquaculture go together in coastal brackish water marshes rich in organic matter.

name: Pokkali Rice
description: Pokkali is a unique saline tolerant rice variety that is cultivated using extensive aquaculture in an organic way in the water-logged coastal regions, spread in about 5000 hectares area in Alappuzha, Kottayam, Thrissur and Ernakulam districts of Kerala in Southern India. The brand Pokkali has received a GI tag from…

name: Trivandrum sadya
description: Trivandrum sadhya or Thiruvananthapuram sadhya is a traditional vegetarian feast that holds significant cultural importance in Thiruvananthapuram, the capital of Kerala. Sadhya is eaten across Kerala, and the Trivandrum sadhya is known for its distinct combination of dishes and flavors.

name: Padayani
description: Padayani, also known Padeni (from the Malayalam word for military formations), is a traditional folk dance and a ritual art from the central portion of the Indian state of Kerala. A ceremonial dance involving masks, it is an ancient ritual performed in Bhagavati temples.

name: Sree Narayana Jayanthi Boat Race
description: The Sree Narayana Jayanthi Vallam Kali or Boat Race, at Kumarakom, Kerala, India is held in September every year during Onam festival.

name: CMS Press, Kottayam
description: C.M.S. Press was the first malayalam printing press in Kerala, India. It was established in 1821 by Rev.

name: Edakkal caves
description: The Edakkal caves are two natural caves at a remote location in Sultan Bathery in the Wayanad district of Kerala in India. They lie 1,200 m (3,900 ft) above sea level on Ambukutty Mala, near an ancient trade route connecting the high mountains of Mysore to the ports of the Malabar Coast.
